findings.title: Conditional serializer method missing `?` so it never runs
findings.body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb defines `def include_website_name` without a question mark. ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_website_name?` (as used for every other conditional attribute in this file, e.g. `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`). Because the name does not match, the gate is never called, so `website_name` is always serialized even when `website` is blank/nil, contrary to intent.

findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 untrusted-attribute hiding
findings.body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb adds `:website_name` to `attributes` but does not add it to `untrusted_attributes` (which hides `website`, `bio_*`, `location`, etc. from anonymous viewers for TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`). Its own `include_website_name` check only tests `website.present?`. As a result a TL0 user's website host/path is still exposed via `website_name` even when `website` itself is correctly suppressed.

findings.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and can crash on nil hostname
findings.body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb `website_name` compares `URI(website.to_s).host == Discourse.current_hostname` and calls `discourse_host.split` / `ends_with?` without normalizing or nil-guarding. DNS hosts are case-insensitive, so `Example.COM` vs `example.com` fails to match and falls through to the host-only branch. If `Discourse.current_hostname` is nil/empty the splits raise NoMethodError, breaking user serialization.
